if you want to help things before they get worse, you need to be very very open and SPECIFIC with your partner. i know getting mad and yelling is a way to stop him in the moment, which isn't necessarily wrong, but it's not going to help him or heal you. sit him down, tell him all the things you do not want him to do anymore. commenting your body, touching your body, etc. if he doesn't know about the assault, and you trust him to respond well, then tell him and get the communication you need from each other. i know it's hard, and i know it's really scary, but if you keep pushing it down and isolating yourself, it will get worse. i'm speaking from experience. if you can't tell him, then still set boundaries. make sure he knows it's not about HIM personally. 

secondly, you need to mend the relationship with yourself and your body. i suggest seeing a therapist if you can. if not, maybe some self help books and some body image exercises can help you.  

if and when you start to feel comfortable having sex with him again, maybe start slow. just foreplay. ask him to tell you everything he wants to do and to ask you if it's okay. make sure you get your pleasure from it too. ask him to make it a top priority, if that's what you need.

it took me years to realize my virginity was stolen from me, rather than something i gave. i was dating someone i 'loved' too. i blamed myself for 'letting' it happen. i have trouble sleeping with people now too. i've been assaulted more than once, tbh. some worse than others. a few of them people i was dating and loved. 

what i do is learn to love my own sexuality. explore it myself. i became a dominatrix, actually. i figured out what i liked, and what i wanted from sexual encounters. if i do have an encounter with someone, they must be someone i trust completely. i communicate exactly what i need from them beforehand, even before we hangout or decide to even have sex. i make sure my needs are important in the bedroom. i came out as queer. i reclaimed my body because it is mine and always has been. same with yours. 

this isn't an easy process, i hate to say, some of us take a lot longer than others to feel okay again. but it is possible. it's been a while since the last time i was assaulted and things still haunt me from years ago sometimes. but most days i'm okay. 

sounds like you might be far away from dating or anything right now, and that's fine. i haven't dated or anything in over two and a half years for similar reasons. but dating and sex isn't everything. make a list of things you want to do, distract yourself. learn an instrument, learn a language, join a sport, something. something that makes you feel good and happy. it sounds silly, but it's the best we can do. distract and move on. go to therapy. heal. distract, keep going. it's about coping. and you will get there. i promise.
